bias_direction: I am biased toward my own prior output. The adversarial critique I authored earlier in this same session is cited three times here as supporting evidence (F1, F2, F7), and I did not subject it to independent challenge before leaning on it. I am also biased toward the conclusion that the apparatus should stop growing, because I arrived at that conclusion first and then measured; the measurements confirmed it, but they were not gathered blind. A third bias runs the other way and is worth naming: proposing a freeze on new workplan files is self-serving in reverse, since it makes my own critique the last document of its kind admitted before the rule takes effect.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer could reasonably argue that Decision 2 is the wrong instrument entirely. A freeze enforced by a check that blocks new checks is still apparatus, added to a repository whose diagnosed illness is too much apparatus, and it will itself generate exemption requests, edge cases and corrective sessions. The stronger form of the objection is that no mechanical rule was ever needed: the owner can simply decline to open meta-sessions, which costs one line of intent and zero code. On Decision 1 the counterclaim is that the quarantine is over-cautious. The 42 determination-bearing names are mostly code-derived values that any competent researcher would rediscover in the first hour of searching, so treating them as contamination may discard genuine coverage information and slow the batch it is meant to protect, in exchange for guarding against an anchoring effect that has not been demonstrated to occur.
